title: Rustamid dynasty
capsule: The Rustamid dynasty was an Ibadi imamate of Persian origin founded c. 777–778 by Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam at Tahert (modern Tiaret, Algeria), established after Ibadi forces expelled from Kairouan regrouped in the central Maghreb. The imamate governed a diverse population of Berber, Arab, and other communities with a reputation for religious tolerance, and served as a hub for Saharan caravan trade connecting sub-Saharan Africa to the Mediterranean. In 909, Fatimid armies under Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i destroyed Tahert and killed or scattered the last Rustamid rulers, driving Ibadi survivors into the Mzab region of Algeria and to Djerba, where Ibadi communities persist today.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Rustamid heartland at Tahert is well attested in Ibadi chronicles and Arabic geographical literature; the full extent of tributary or commercial influence across the Sahara lacks archaeological corroboration and is approximated.
